messages:
amira: Quick follow-up from the autoscaler RFC — I'm worried our current operator-only admission model makes it hard to reason about prewarm costs and KV-cache priming across tenants. Can we sketch a clear boundary for admission vs runtime responsibilities?

sam: +1. We need a clean contract so control plane can charge/credit customers and operator can execute without guessing.

joel: What do you mean by "charge/credit" here? billing vs warmup accounting?

amira: billing + accounting. For example: tenant A triggers a burst, control plane issues a prewarm hint; operator starts instances and populates KV cache. Who gets billed for that prewarm time if the tenant never actually sends queries?

olivia: Two obvious options: 1) Control-plane creates a prewarm reservation that deducts credits immediately. 2) Operator performs opportunistic prewarm and reports usage retrospectively. Both have tradeoffs.

sam: Option 1 is simpler for predictability (immediate charge), but hurts user experience when hints are noisy. Option 2 is nicer for UX but opens us to cost leakage unless we have strong guardrails.

joel: Also want to call out cold-start vs KV priming. A prewarmed VM without a hot KV cache still feels cold for long context workloads. We should separate compute warmup and cache warmup in the contract.

amira: Agreed. Suggest we define three surfaces in the contract: 1) Admission intent (control-plane -> operator): tokens include prewarm_type (compute|cache|both), ttl, tenant_id, tentative_cost. 2) Execution acknowledgment (operator -> control-plane): accepted/rejected + estimated start_time. 3) Settled usage (operator -> control-plane): actual seconds billed and cache-priming bytes.

sam: That maps well to billing flows. Could be a small JSON handshake:```json
{"tenant_id":"t123","intent_id":"i-456","prewarm_type":"cache","ttl_s":300,"expected_cost_cents":12}
```

olivia: We also need telemetry keys to avoid disputes: prewarm_hint_id, cache_checksum/version, list of primed model shards. Metrics: `prewarm_hints`, `prewarm_accepted`, `prewarm_rejected`, `cache_primed_bytes`, `cache_hit_ramp_t50`.

joel: Operationally, operator should be allowed to reject or throttle hints when GPU pressure is high. Rejection reasons should be enumerated: capacity, safety, policy_quota. Control-plane can retry or fallback to lower-quality model variants.

amira: Good call. That implies the control-plane must be able to request cheaper variants as part of the intent. Add `fallback_model_priority` field.

sam: One more wrinkle: multi-tenant GPU slices (shared devices) where priming one tenant's model benefits others. How do we attribute priming cost?

olivia: Hmm. We could attribute proportionally by later usage (retrospective charge split), or we could keep a shared pool credit that teams top up for opportunistic priming. Both are heavy.

joel: For MVP, prefer conservative approach: only allow control-plane-allocated prewarms for dedicated reservations. Opportunistic operator prewarms on shared pools should be disabled or charged to a shared warming budget with tight caps.

amira: Sounds reasonable. Action items: sam to prototype the handshake schema and draft billing flow; joel to sketch operator reject reasons + retry semantics; olivia to enumerate telemetry metrics. I'll collect into a short RFC follow-up doc.

sam: I'll spin up a small prototype PR with the JSON handshake and a stubbed metric set. ETA EOD Friday.

orch-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orch/pull/789 — "prewarm-handshake-proto" :robot_face:

olivia: Nice. One more ask — include a TTL-based eviction signal so control-plane can indicate when primed caches are safe to evict without customer-facing errors.

joel: Also add a `consistency_level` enum (best_effort | tenant_strict) for cache priming. Operator can use that to prefer cheaper shard priming for best_effort.

amira: Perfect. We'll sync Friday 10am to review the PR and make a decision on retrospective billing vs upfront charge for the MVP. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
